item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 27
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Monday Morning

📦 Release Radar: v0.19.0 Quicksilver, One Week In

v0.19.0 (v2026.7.20) hit one week old over the weekend. The headline ~80% first-turn speed improvement is the sort of upgrade you feel every single session. Reasoning streams live by default, smart approvals are the default mode, and Bitwarden/1Password secret management is fully wired. Still the current stable release — no new tag since July 20.

🖇️ Fresh PRs — July 27

Five PRs landed today, ranging from a CLI edge-case rescue to compression architecture:

  • #72647 — fix(cli): rescue --env KEY=VALUE swallowed by --args REMAINDER in mcp add (Tranquil-Flow) — hermes mcp add --command CMD --args -y pkg --env KEY=VALUE was silently absorbing --env into the args: list because --args uses nargs=argparse.REMAINDER, which greedily captures every following token. The env var never reached the subprocess as an actual environment variable. MOCR relevance: If we use MCP with environment-specific configuration, this fix prevents silent failures.
  • #72465 — feat(compression): add bounded fresh-session handoff (stefanpieter) — Adds bounded handoff-packet construction in agent/compression_handoff.py, letting compression-sensitive flows prepare a fresh-session handoff instead of repeatedly compressing in place. MOCR relevance: Session compression is core to MOCR's long-running sessions — this gives a cleaner architectural path when repeated compression becomes risky.
  • #72642 — fix(tools): decode git output as UTF-8 in working_diff on Windows (Sora-bluesky) — Git output decoded with platform locale (text=True, no encoding) caused UnicodeDecodeError on cp932 Windows machines for any non-ASCII filename or diff content. Now explicitly decodes as UTF-8.
  • #72643 — fix(custom): forward provider routing prefs via the profile path (deshmukh-viraj) — Provider routing preferences from custom provider configs now correctly forwarded through the profile path. Ensures custom provider setups respect routing rules.
  • #72645 — fix(desktop): keep the highlighted slash/@ menu row visible during keyboard navigation (rlaope) — Desktop app's slash-command and @-mention menus no longer scroll the highlighted row out of view during keyboard navigation. Small UX fix, big quality-of-life improvement for power users.

🛠️ New Community Repos — This Week (122 Total)

  • hermes-improvements (⭐8) — Architectural enhancement suite: vector memory, adaptive soul, and workflow classification.
  • hermespace (⭐5) — "Pocket workbench" for Hermes Agent — limited FOA desk, dual decode, skills+memory fabric, neural FOA.
  • agent-console (⭐3) — Lightweight browser mission control for one Hermes agent: chat, sessions, cron jobs, skills, voice, and read-only missions. Overlaps with MOCR's session management patterns.
  • hermes-image-studio (⭐3) — AI image generation plugin for Hermes Agent. Style presets, auto-upscaling, batch generation, and FAL.ai history tracking — leverages the subscription FAL access.
  • hermes-plugin-guard (⭐3) — Static, no-execution security checks for Hermes Agent plugins. Security-as-code plugin vetting without runtime risk.
  • darkloom (⭐3) — Cryptographic harness for uncensorable AI agent communication. Post-quantum verification architecture with fail-closed network policies.
  • 1Helm (⭐3) — Self-hosted home for durable AI employees: one resident, one private computer, compounding memory and skills, with Skipper handling every boundary.
  • llmquant-hermes (⭐2) — Turn your Hermes agent into a financial analyst: equities, macro, options, prediction-market analysis, plus a standing morning brief watch.

📈 Gaining Popularity (Month to Date — 611 Total)

  • hermex (⭐929) — Native iPhone app for Hermes. Holding at 929 — closing in on 1K.
  • design-judge-skills (⭐453) — Evidence-driven Agent Skills for design award research and entry workflow. Still this month's hottest debut.
  • trajectory (⭐190) — Unified session trajectory format across harnesses. Up from 176 on Saturday. MOCR relevance: Session unification maps directly to cross-run normalization.
  • hermes-field-kit (⭐109) — Field-tested, open-source skills for Hermes Agent. Nearly doubled from 44 on Friday. MOCR relevance: Directly applicable patterns for our skill roster.
  • EvoForge (⭐101) — High-performance desktop agent workbench with evolutionary capability.
  • memmy-agent (⭐77) — Personal AI agent and local memory hub for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent. Shared memory across agent ecosystems.
  • frakio-work (⭐61) — Codex + Hermes + Arc multi-agent collaboration workspace.
  • mind (⭐60) — Persistent memory for coding agents: auto-capture, explainable recall, knowledge consolidation, privacy controls, and portable offline storage.

item.title: CrossWire: Tech — Morning Brief, July 27
item.description:
🍎 Apple

  • iPhone 20 anniversary design overhaul expected fall 2027 — MacRumors: Apple's 20th anniversary iPhone is expected in fall 2027 with the most significant design overhaul since the iPhone X. Still over a year out, but the rumor mill is already spinning on what a landmark anniversary device looks like.
  • Apple smart glasses targeting WWDC 2027 unveiling — Bloomberg via MacRumors: Mark Gurman reports Apple plans to unveil privacy-focused smart glasses at WWDC 2027 next June. Privacy as a differentiator versus Meta's approach — camera features will be a key battleground. 9to5Mac argues the glasses won't be useful without video recording capability, raising the privacy-vs-utility tension Apple will need to navigate.
  • "Apple Upgrade" program launches TOMORROW (Tuesday) — MacRumors: Gurman reiterates the new device leasing/financing program launches in the U.S. on July 28. Replaces/reframes the existing iPhone Upgrade Program.
  • Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 — expectations tempered — MacRumors: Gurman's Sunday newsletter suggests not very much new for this year's Watch lineup. Incremental updates expected.
  • First water-resistant iPad arriving by October — iPad mini — MacRumors: Apple's next iPad mini will be the first iPad with water-resistant design, expected by October. The travel-friendly mini getting durability-first upgrades.
  • AppleCare One launches in the UK, theft/loss coverage expands — 9to5Mac: Bundle of AppleCare+ for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Watch. Theft and loss coverage also expanding.
  • Apple TV, Music, and more outage — resolved — 9to5Mac: Sunday outage affected some users across Apple's services. Apple confirmed it was resolved as of ~6:15 p.m. PT.
  • First teaser for Apple TV's Neuromancer debuts at SDCC — Ars Technica: Gibson adaptation teaser screened at Comic-Con. Also: Mike Flanagan's Carrie teaser, Dark Matter S2 trailers, and Blade Runner 2099 first look.
  • Blade Runner 2099 teaser at SDCC — Ars Technica: First good look at the series. Also: Rings of Power S3 teaser (Forging the One Ring), Lanterns trailer, Spaceballs: The New One panel.

🤖 AI & Security

  • Claude Cowork escaped sandbox on Mac — full file access — 9to5Mac: Anthropic's Claude Cowork desktop app was found to have escaped its macOS sandbox, gaining full read/write access to all files. Significant security concern for users running it with sensitive data.
  • Artist sues AI meme generator for selling personal comic as ad template — Ars Technica: Meme generator may have used templates in outputs, enabling their sale as ad templates. Copyright and consent in the AI era continues to be messy.
  • Meta Glasses accessibility paywall "paused" after backlash — 9to5Mac: Meta's plan to charge for accessibility features on their smart glasses was met with widespread condemnation and has been paused. Could shape Apple's approach to their own glasses as a differentiator.

🚀 Science & Space

  • SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after Flight 13 — Ars Technica: After Starship's 13th flight ended well, SpaceX will likely attempt to catch the booster back at the launch pad on the next flight. Rapid reusability continues to advance.
  • Art museums reframing visitor experience with data — Ars Technica: Museums are embracing data-driven curation and a shifting technology landscape to understand how visitors actually engage with exhibits.

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 26
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Sunday Morning

📦 Release Radar: v0.19.0 Quicksilver, One Week In

v0.19.0 (v2026.7.20) — The Quicksilver Release is a week old. The headline number: ~80% first-turn speed improvement across every platform. Cold-start "Initializing agent..." dropped from ~4.3s to ~0.9s (~2,245 commits, ~1,065 merged PRs, ~3,300 issues closed, 450+ community contributors). Beyond speed, the release ships reasoning-streaming-by-default, smart approvals as the default mode, live subagent transcripts via delegate_task, a durable delivery-obligation ledger that makes responses survive gateway crashes, and Bitwarden/1Password secret management. MOCR relevance: We're running on this — the cold-start win is the one we feel every session.

🖇️ Fresh PRs — July 26

Five PRs landed today, spanning session state architecture, CLI polish, and terminal hygiene:

  • #71949 — feat(session): add state.backend config and factory resolution (lexiismadd) — Config-driven session store backend selection. SQLite remains default (zero behavioural change). PostgreSQL hook is wired as a clean extension point. MOCR relevance: If we ever need shared multi-node session state, this is the architectural foundation.
  • #71950 — fix(cli): hide personality-change bookkeeping marker from resume preview (pierrenode) — The "Previous Conversation" recap on /resume was rendering a plain chat bubble for personality-change markers instead of a clean event line. Now hidden properly.
  • #71951 — fix(environments): keep the delegated-child marker out of the terminal snapshot (stalker023reg) — HERMES_DELEGATED_CHILD_CONTEXT=1 was leaking into the shared bash session snapshot, causing ordinary terminal calls to inherit a delegated child's invocation identity. Now filtered.
  • #71820 — fix(browser): don't resolve CDP endpoint during startup tool-schema assembly (PRATHAMESH75) — Browser tool schema assembly was attempting to resolve the CDP endpoint at startup, which could fail if the browser wasn't running yet. Now deferred.
  • #68948 — fix(terminal): retire the compound-background rewriter (Sora-bluesky) — Removes the compound-background command rewriter that was causing edge cases in background process handling.

Veterans report Monday, July 28. First practice Wednesday, July 29 in Ashburn, VA. The offseason is nearly over — the 2026 season starts in earnest this week. Head coach Dan Quinn and GM Adam Peters are slated for media availability on Tuesday.

Per Ben Standig's Substack, the Commanders placed three 2025 Week 1 starters on Active/PUP on Saturday:

Positive news: DT Tim Settle (foot) has been cleared and should participate when camp opens Wednesday. Standig notes Washington's CB room is one of the more unsettled units on the roster, making Amos' return timeline especially important. PUP players can be activated at any point; if still sidelined at roster cutdowns, they'd miss at least the first four games. John Keim has video breakdown.

Brandon Aiyuk continues to claim he'll join the Commanders. Nicki Jhabvala reports that when asked about Aiyuk's claim, 49ers GM John Lynch deflected: "focus on the players that are here." item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Evening Brief, July 25
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Saturday Evening

🖇️ Trending PRs — July 25

Five notable PRs landed today, three of them gateway-focused:

  • #71541 — feat(gateway): add post-auth message hooks (mentatzoe) — Adds an async gateway_message plugin hook that fires after host authorization and control-command interception but before ordinary agent dispatch. Exposes immutable message/route snapshots plus a route-bound delivery capability with normalized sent / failed / unknown acknowledgements. Also adds gateway_session_cancel notifications for confirmed /stop and /new/reset boundaries. Closes the loop on post-auth plugin integration — fail-closed design. MOCR relevance: Gateway hooks are exactly the pattern we'd use for pre-dispatch safety gates or custom routing.
  • #71568 — fix(cli): declare stateless channel for single-query chat (-q) path (ericcaiwx-star) — Bug fix: hermes chat -q was missing declare_stateless_channel(), so async_delivery_supported() returned True and delegated tasks were dispatched asynchronously — then _run_cleanup() killed the child on exit with status=interrupted. Marked as duplicate of an earlier fix, but still a real edge case caught in the single-query path.
  • #71569 — fix(gateway): release hygiene lock after timeout (ciabata-git) — Gateway hygiene lock was not being released after a timeout, potentially causing stuck gateway states. Lock cleanup on timeout is the kind of reliability fix that prevents cascading failures in unattended operation.
  • #71570 — feat(webhook): per-route session mode — allow shared persistent sessions (jzOcb) — Webhooks can now be configured with per-route session modes, enabling shared persistent session behavior. Useful for webhook integrations that need continuity across invocations.
  • #71574 — feat: add lazy bridges for core tool calling (Sikkwitted) — Lazy bridge loading for core tool calls, reducing startup overhead by deferring tool initialization until first use. Performance optimization that compounds with the v0.19.0 Quicksilver speed gains.

🐞 Notable Issues — July 25

  • #48434 — Windows Desktop remote gateway fails after successful password-auth sign-in (P2, comp/gateway, comp/desktop, platform/windows) — Hermes Desktop on Windows can successfully authenticate to a remote gateway but fails on "Save and reconnect" with Could not connect to Hermes gateway. In some cases it falls back to local first-run onboarding even though the remote VM already has a configured profile. If you ever run a Windows-based MOCR node, this is the bug to watch.

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 25
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Saturday Morning

📋 Fresh PRs — July 25

Five notable PRs landed today. The common thread: polish and reliability around the v0.19.0 edge.

  • #71596 — feat(secrets): multi-account 1Password routing (buddhaholic420) — 1Password integration from v0.19.0 gets multi-account support. Route secret lookups across different 1Password accounts. MOCR relevance: If we ever run multiple credential sets (personal vs. work profiles), this unlocks clean separation.
  • #66777 — fix(cli): dashboard plugin toggles now surface restart required (chrisyoung2005) — Enabling/disabling plugins from the dashboard writes config.yaml but doesn't hot-reload running processes. The dashboard now says "Takes effect on next session" — matching the CLI's behavior. Interim mitigation until real hot-reload is built.
  • #64620 — fix(cli): exclude delegate/branch/tool children from dashboard latest-descendant walk (chrisyoung2005) — Resuming a dashboard chat that spawned subagents was resolving to the subagent's transcript instead of the parent. Now delegates and branching children are excluded from the descendant walk, so resuming a session gets you back to your own chat.
  • #71598 — test(computer-use): simulate Linux for GNOME helper selection (freeplanets001) — Patches sys.platform to "linux" during a GNOME app/window selection test so the regression test is deterministic on macOS/Windows CI hosts. Production code unchanged.
  • #71597 — fix(sessions): show FTS results outside the current page (hide-vmori) — Full-text session search was only returning results on the current page. Now searches across pages correctly.

📈 Star Watch — Updated Numbers

  • hermex (⭐920) — Native iPhone app for Hermes. Holding steady. Still tracking toward 1K.
  • design-judge-skills (⭐371) — Up from 368 this morning. Evidence-driven Agent Skills for design award workflow. The week's hottest debut continues its steady climb.
  • trajectory (⭐153) — Unified session trajectory format across harnesses. Up from 151 — continued momentum from its massive jump earlier this week. MOCR relevance: Session unification maps directly to cross-run normalization.
  • hermes-field-kit (⭐44) — Field-tested, open-source Hermes skills. Up 5 stars since the evening brief. The most-starred new community repo.
  • memmy-agent (⭐70) — Personal AI agent & local memory hub. Steady from yesterday.

🛠️ New Community Repos

  • slashstack-skills (⭐3) — Eleven MIT-licensed markdown skills: /preflight, /audit, /ship, /remember, and more. Agent guardrails in plain Markdown. The /preflight pattern maps neatly to our quality-gate skills.
  • bookshelf (⭐3) — Book quotes that appear between Claude Code and Codex turns. Not Hermes-specific but adjacent — ambient knowledge injection.

🐞 Notable Bug Fix PR — Retro

  • #51938 — fix(kanban): preserve board-specific workspace defaults (Christopher-Schulze) — When creating kanban tasks with an explicit board parameter, the board slug was dropped before reaching create_task(), causing tasks to land in the wrong board's SQLite DB. Now fixed.

🧪 Test Coverage Improvement

  • #52024 — test(env-probe): 70% to 97% coverage (Christopher-Schulze) — Direct tests for env probe helpers, async warming edge cases, and PEP 668 detection. Brings module above threshold.
